Forevane — market, product, and design research

Research date: 17 September 2026. Audience: founders, product, design, engineering, and early community partners. All observations below are based on public first-party pages inspected during this session. Product claims on other companies' pages are their own claims; they have not been independently audited. This is a qualitative comparison of recognizable onchain products, not a traffic or market-share ranking.

1. What Outrive actually does

Outrive describes itself as bringing Hyperliquid prediction markets into Telegram. Its core promise is “Your view. Your move.” The user discovers a market, chooses a side and order type, places an order, and shares a call. Other group members can tail the same side or fade the opposite side in a private Telegram flow, with their own position size. Discord supports discovery, search, categories, deployers, and charts; trading is in Telegram.

The Calls documentation distinguishes filled orders from resting limit orders. Filled calls show an actual average fill; resting calls show the intended limit price. Rejected orders cannot become calls. Calls retain history after expiry and do not reveal private trade size or wallet addresses by default. These details matter more than copying its colors: the product makes a social opinion actionable while preserving the distinction between a statement, an order, and a fill.

The Start guide says the bot creates or refreshes an Outrive wallet; its deposit instructions specify native USDC on Arbitrum and Hyperliquid deposits. The Vault guide adds a five-minute browser/passkey approval flow for withdrawals and private-key export, while trading remains in the bot. Forevane should not inherit a bot-managed-key model merely to look similar.

The fee table lists a 0.25% fee below $1,000 rolling 30-day volume, stepping down to 0.10% at $500,000+. The fee applies to notional value when a position is sold or closed through the bot. That monetization depends on real execution volume and financial activity; it is not a suitable revenue assumption for a no-stakes forecasting prototype.

Transferable insight: communities are a distribution channel, a context layer, and a reason to return. A call needs a clear state and history. Original Forevane wedge: make a forecast inspectable before it becomes a reputation claim: question, deadline, fixed resolution source, YES/NO, confidence, wallet, transaction, and eventual outcome. Start with a portable public record, without deposits, trading, or financial prizes.

2. Robinhood Chain: capabilities and constraints

The official introduction describes a permissionless EVM-compatible Layer 2 built with Arbitrum Dedicated Blockchains, ETH gas, first-come-first-served sequencing, and ERC-4337 account abstraction. It emphasizes tokenized real-world assets. These capabilities support ordinary Solidity contracts and wallet interactions; they do not mean a new application has Robinhood distribution, endorsement, licensing, liquidity, or a prediction-market settlement service.

The network configuration published at the time of research is:

Property Testnet used by the prototype Mainnet, future evaluation only
Chain ID 46630 4663
Gas ETH ETH
Public RPC https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com
Explorer https://explorer.testnet.chain.robinhood.com https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com

Official docs warn that public RPC endpoints are rate-limited and are not recommended for production. Use a paid/provider endpoint, event indexing, and monitoring before a public launch. Network parameters must be rechecked at release time.

Oracle documentation identifies Chainlink feeds and requires careful interpretation: a Stock Token's price includes its corporate-action multiplier and can differ from the underlying headline share price; stock feeds run 24/5; corporate actions can pause feeds; stale data and sequencer downtime must be handled. Consequently “Will NVDA finish above $X?” is incomplete unless it names the instrument, source, observation time, time zone, adjustment convention, and cancellation rule. The prototype uses an explicitly disclosed owner-resolved process, not an invented decentralized oracle.

The Robinhood Chain product page states that Stock Tokens are tokenized debt securities, do not confer rights in the underlying issuer, and are unavailable in the US with other geographic restrictions. Forevane's initial no-stakes market commentary must not be marketed as access to Stock Tokens, a Robinhood account, or a licensed execution service. No Robinhood affiliation is claimed.

3. Website benchmark: content, layout, style, and adaptation

Browser screenshots are saved in output/playwright/research-*.png. Public HTML snapshots are retained in this research directory for source traceability. Some live sites displayed data placeholders until client-side APIs loaded; those placeholders are not performance or adoption evidence.

Site Observed content and hierarchy Observed visual language Useful pattern for Forevane
Outrive Single clear promise; product call card; three-step flow; interactive example; community entry points; order/wallet details; FAQ Charcoal and amber, oversized bold sans-serif, large brand gesture, cream information card, strong horizontal rules Explain a call visually; keep factual status on the card; illustrate the social loop; retain one clear primary action
Hyperliquid Broad finance thesis; direct Trade/Build routes; market breadth; technical and ecosystem evidence Current homepage uses pale background, dark green type, mint buttons, large serif headline, compact pill navigation, generous whitespace Use an editorial opening and decisive CTA; keep technical proof reachable; replace established-brand statistics with verifiable prototype facts
Jupiter App-first home; persistent Trade/Earn/Manage sidebar; search; wallet control; central swap module; campaign and portfolio panels Near-black interface, dense but grouped controls, lime highlights, rounded surfaces, clearly interactive product Make the first user action available on the landing page; place wallet/network state beside it; progressive disclosure for detailed rules
Pendle “Liberating Yield”; distinction between Boros margin and V2 spot; numeric proof section; education/resources Full-screen dark hero, moving wireframe/spherical artwork, restrained blue accent, short rotating headline, high contrast One memorable motion system can establish identity; show product modes clearly; provide educational depth below the fold
Morpho “Open credit network”; explicit embedded earn, loans and curator solutions; developer links; audits, formal verification and noncustodial explanation Black hero with a blue particle sphere, centered promise, restrained navigation, generous spacing, solution blocks, and security evidence separated from marketing Explain value by customer role; put verifiability, risk and administration information in discoverable sections; only show audits after one exists

These are different business models: Hyperliquid is trading infrastructure, Jupiter is an integrated product interface, Pendle specializes in yield, Morpho supplies lending infrastructure, and Outrive is a social execution layer. Their scale claims cannot be transplanted to Forevane.

4. Selected direction and original design brief

Position: a social forecasting record on Robinhood Chain. Line: “Your next take. On the record.” Product grammar: discover → inspect → choose a side and confidence → commit with a wallet → revisit the outcome. A strong opinion becomes a record that can be checked, including wrong calls.

Use a bright pale-mint canvas with charcoal text, a disciplined grid, large editorial headings, and original metallic signal artwork. The conceptual visual is a direction indicator carrying a durable record: motion, conviction, and accountability. It must be visibly different from Outrive's amber paper-plane motif. Mint is a Forevane design choice, not a use of Robinhood or Hyperliquid branding.

The homepage should combine Hyperliquid's spacious hierarchy with Jupiter's immediate product access. Above the fold: concise promise, testnet status, one primary “Explore calls” action, wallet access, and an original hero object. Follow with a functional call board, the three-step record loop, why a timestamp matters, the trust/resolution model, a community roadmap, and clear FAQs. Richness should come from real interaction, thoughtful typography, rule details, and complete states rather than invented statistics.

Interaction and accessibility requirements

  • Browsing works without a wallet. Wallet connection is requested when a user chooses to submit or inspect their records.
  • A call shows its deadline, resolution source, state, and owner-resolution disclosure before submission. Display network and testnet status at the transaction step.
  • Confidence describes the user's forecast, not a quoted market probability or expected return. Audience percentages are illustrative unless derived from real eligible records.
  • Distinguish disconnected, wrong network, awaiting signature, pending transaction, confirmed, rejected, expired, cancelled, and unavailable states. A rejected signature must never produce a successful record.
  • Motion supports hierarchy; respect reduced-motion preferences. Use keyboard-accessible dialogs and controls, visible focus, readable contrast, and useful mobile touch targets.
  • Existing transactions and event reads are the source of truth. Locally remembered wallet state is convenience, not authentication or a claim of successful onchain submission.
  • No fabricated TVL, trade volume, user counts, partnership marks, audit badges, APYs, or earnings claims.

5. Commercial interpretation

Forevane should sell a workflow to community operators: structured forecasting rounds, reliable recaps, and an exportable history that makes community discussion more useful. Individual users receive a record they can take across communities. The first paid hypothesis is community subscriptions, supported by an optional individual analysis tier. API licensing comes later after data integrity and customer demand are demonstrated.

The chain alone is not a moat. The potential advantages are a useful recurring community ritual, normalized question/resolution data, distribution through original communities, reliable all-calls history, and accumulated long-term forecast calibration. Wallets do not prove unique people, and an onchain timestamp does not prove a forecast was honestly resolved. Product claims and the operating model must reflect those limits.

6. Decision log

  1. Adapt Outrive's social loop, not its assets or copy. No copied code, images, logo, or proprietary design files.
  2. Start with no-stakes forecasting, which is independently useful without building liquidity or a trading venue.
  3. Make owner resolution a prominent testnet limitation; implement fixed rules and cancellation handling; do not call it trustless.
  4. Restrict the first product to finite, objectively resolvable questions. Avoid ambiguous breaking-news markets and topics with personal harm incentives.
  5. Offer subscriptions for workflow and analysis. No token sale, transaction-fee forecast, or airdrop promise in the base plan.
  6. Treat any future execution integration as a separate legal, technical, and commercial decision.
